answer: A farm must thus either lie, which the basalt graph proves on replay, or recruit 91 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the ridge registry records each claim and the ledge audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 33% of the attester's bond. That is 32 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
